answer: Resist Sybil farms with correlated-behavior cluster slashing. The network compares timing, task choices, and output patterns across identities, like tracing timber from one forest: fakes grown together leave matching grain. When a cluster looks too alike, each member must pass an independent check, not rest on a shared relic of past work. Failures slash the whole cluster's earnings, so one exposed fake poisons its siblings. Attackers must run every fake diversely and continuously, paying coordination costs per fake, while honest agents keep the nectar of rewards for genuine, varied work.
